note: Every card line restates the quoted text of an official page (sources[*].page, sources[*].quote), read 1 November 2026. Written for the web-design and Salesforce city pages; no client, office or result is claimed.

filing.line: LLCs and corporations file an annual report with the Kentucky Secretary of State by June 30 each year, with a $15 filing fee.

privacy.line: In force since 1 January 2026 (KRS 367.3611 to 367.3629), it reaches businesses that handle personal data of 100,000 Kentucky consumers, or 25,000 while earning half their revenue from selling data.

tax.h3: Sales tax on the build itself
tax.line: KRS 139.200 lists website design and development services, and website hosting, among the services Kentucky taxes at 6%, so ask your accountant how it lands on the invoice.

breach.line: A business must tell Kentucky residents when their unencrypted personal information is taken, or reasonably believed taken, in a breach of its systems.

Kentucky.lead: A Kentucky site that sells or takes enquiries meets all three: the tax line on the build, the privacy notice and the breach duty.
Kentucky.crm: Kentucky's consumer data law took effect on 1 January 2026, and it covers the customer records a Salesforce org holds once a business crosses its thresholds.

ky-sos.name: Kentucky Secretary of State
ky-sos.what: Annual reports: due date and filing fee
ky-sos.quote: are required to file annual reports with this office by June 30 of each year. ... Your annual report must be signed, dated and accompanied by a $15 filing fee.

ky-ag.name: Office of the Kentucky Attorney General
ky-ag.quote: The Kentucky Consumer Data Protection Act ("KCDPA") went into effect on January 1, 2026. The KCDPA is codified in KRS 367.3611 to 367.3629

ky-tax.name: Kentucky General Assembly, KRS 139.200
ky-tax.quote: A tax is hereby imposed upon all retailers at the rate of six percent (6%) of the gross receipts derived from: ... (v) Website design and development services; (w) Website hosting services;

ky-breach.name: Kentucky General Assembly, KRS 365.732
ky-breach.quote: (2) Any information holder shall disclose any breach of the security of the system, following discovery or notification of the breach in the security of the data, to any resident of Kentucky whose unencrypted personal information was, or is reasonably believed to have been, acquired by an unauthorized person.

filing.line: A domestic LLC pays the Department of Financial Institutions $25 to file its annual report online, or $40 on paper.

tax.h3: Web design and Wisconsin sales tax
tax.line: Publication 235 says website design is not a taxable service in Wisconsin, and hosting and domain names are not taxed either; logos, banners or videos sold separately are.

breach.line: When personal information is acquired without authorization, Wisconsin law has the business make reasonable efforts to notify each person it belongs to.

Wisconsin.lead: A Wisconsin site's proposal can price design apart from any logo or video, because the state's own guidance taxes them differently.
Wisconsin.crm: Wisconsin's breach statute, § 134.98, applies to the personal information in a CRM: if it is taken, each person in the records must be told.

wi-dfi.name: Wisconsin Department of Financial Institutions
wi-dfi.quote: Domestic Entities Business Corporation Cooperative (Stock or Membership) Limited Liability Company Limited Liability Partnership Limited Partnership Nonstock Corporation ... Annual Report $40.00 $15.00 $40.00 $25.00 $25.00 $40.00 Annual Report via Online Filing $25.00 $25.00 $25.00

wi-tax.name: Wisconsin Department of Revenue, Publication 235
wi-tax.what: Sales and use tax on computer services and websites
wi-tax.quote: Website design is not among the services subject to Wisconsin sales tax if the service is not primarily a photographic service. ... Note: Charges for web hosting, domain names, data storage, and data processing are not subject to Wisconsin sales or use taxes.

wi-breach.name: Wisconsin State Legislature, § 134.98
wi-breach.what: Notice of unauthorized acquisition of personal information
wi-breach.quote: 134.98 Notice of unauthorized acquisition of personal information. ... the entity shall make reasonable efforts to notify each subject of the personal information.

filing.line: An Oregon LLC renews every year on the anniversary of its original filing, through the Secretary of State's Oregon Business Registry.

privacy.line: ORS 646A.570 to 646A.589 took effect on 1 July 2024 for businesses that process data of 100,000 consumers, or 25,000 with over 25% of revenue from selling it.

breach.line: The Oregon Consumer Information Protection Act sets a firm outer limit for telling Oregon consumers about a breach of their personal information, counted from discovery.

Oregon.lead: Oregon's privacy act asks a covered business for a clear privacy notice and an opt-out route, both of which live on the website.
Oregon.crm: Oregon's Consumer Privacy Act has applied since 1 July 2024, so the contact and consent records in a Salesforce org are in scope once a business crosses its thresholds.

or-sos.name: Oregon Secretary of State, Corporation Division
or-sos.quote: All other business entity types renew every year. Your renewal is due on the anniversary date of the original filing.

or-doj.name: Oregon Department of Justice
or-doj.quote: the Oregon Consumer Privacy Act, ORS 646A.570-646A.589 ... takes effect on July 1, 2024. ... at least 100,000 consumers; or 25,000 or more consumers and derives over 25% of annual gross revenue from the sale of personal data.

or-breach.name: Oregon Department of Justice
or-breach.quote: Oregon law requires entities to notify any Oregon consumer whose personal information was subject to a breach of security within 45 days of discovering the breach of security.

filing.line: A Utah business entity renews with the Division of Corporations and Commercial Code one year after registration and every year after, online at businessregistration.utah.gov.

privacy.line: Utah Code § 13-61-102 applies to businesses with $25,000,000 or more in annual revenue that also handle data of 100,000 Utah consumers, or 25,000 while earning over half their revenue from selling personal data.

breach.line: If an investigation finds that personal information was, or is reasonably likely to be, misused for identity theft or fraud, each affected Utah resident must be told.

Utah.lead: Utah's revenue floor means most small firms sit outside its privacy act, while the breach statute covers every business that keeps personal data.
Utah.crm: Utah's breach statute, § 13-44-202, turns on whether misuse of the records is likely, which is why access and audit settings in a CRM matter.

ut-com.name: Utah Division of Corporations and Commercial Code
ut-com.quote: The renewal is due one year from the date of registration and due annually thereafter

ut-dcp.name: Utah State Legislature, § 13-61-102
ut-dcp.what: Utah Consumer Privacy Act: who it applies to
ut-dcp.quote: (b) has annual revenue of $25,000,000 or more; and (c) satisfies one or more of the following thresholds: (i) during a calendar year, controls or processes personal data of 100,000 or more consumers; or (ii) derives over 50% of the entity's gross revenue from the sale of personal data and controls or processes personal data of 25,000 or more consumers.

ut-breach.name: Utah State Legislature, § 13-44-202
ut-breach.what: Personal information: notice of a breach
ut-breach.quote: (b) If an investigation under Subsection (1)(a) reveals that the misuse of personal information for identity theft or fraud purposes has occurred, or is reasonably likely to occur, the person shall provide notification to each affected Utah resident.

filing.line: A Minnesota LLC files its renewal with the Secretary of State by December 31 of each calendar year, and the statute sets no fee for it.

privacy.line: Minnesota Statutes 325M.10 to 325M.21 took effect on 31 July 2025 for businesses handling data of 100,000 residents, or earning over 25% of revenue from selling data.

breach.line: A business that keeps Minnesotans' personal data must disclose a breach of its system after it discovers it or is told of it.

Minnesota.lead: Minnesota's newest privacy law is the one most likely to change a site's privacy notice, cookie choices and opt-out link.
Minnesota.crm: Minnesota's Consumer Data Privacy Act took effect on 31 July 2025, reaching the customer records a business keeps in Salesforce once it crosses the thresholds.

mn-sos.name: Minnesota Revisor of Statutes, § 322C.0208
mn-sos.quote: A limited liability company must file with the secretary of state by December 31 of each calendar year a renewal ... Notwithstanding section 322C.0205, subdivision 1, no fee is required to file an annual renewal.

mn-ag.name: Office of the Minnesota Attorney General
mn-ag.what: Minnesota Consumer Data Privacy Act takes effect
mn-ag.quote: On July 31st, the Minnesota Consumer Data Privacy Act (MCDPA) takes effect ... Businesses are subject to the Minnesota Consumer Data Privacy Act if they control or process the personal data of 100,000 or more Minnesota residents, or if they earn over 25% of their revenue from the sale of personal data and process or control personal data of 25,000 consumers or more.

mn-breach.name: Minnesota Revisor of Statutes, § 325E.61
mn-breach.quote: DATA WAREHOUSES; NOTICE REQUIRED FOR CERTAIN DISCLOSURES. ... shall disclose any breach of the security of the system following discovery or notification of the breach.

filing.line: For-profit entities file a business entity report with the Secretary of State every other year, in the month they were formed, through INBiz: $31 online or $50 by mail.

privacy.line: IC 24-15 applies from 1 January 2026 to businesses that handle data of 100,000 Indiana consumers, or 25,000 while earning over half their revenue from selling it.

tax.h3: Web design and Indiana sales tax
tax.line: Indiana's Sales Tax Information Bulletin 8 treats web design as a service outside sales and use tax, as long as no tangible property changes hands, and hosting as well.

breach.line: The Attorney General's guidance says affected consumers must be told without unreasonable delay once a breach is discovered.

Indiana.lead: Indiana's privacy act began in 2026, so a site built before then may need a new privacy notice and an opt-out route.
Indiana.crm: Indiana's Consumer Data Protection Act has applied since 1 January 2026, which brings the customer records in a CRM into scope above its thresholds.

in-sos.name: Indiana Secretary of State, Business Services Division
in-sos.quote: For-profit entities file every other year (biennial) in the anniversary month in which the entity was originally created. ... For Profit by Mail: $50 ... For Profit Online: $31

in-cdpa.name: Indiana General Assembly, IC 24-15
in-cdpa.quote: Sec. 1. (a) This article applies to a person that conducts business in Indiana or produces products or services that are targeted to residents of Indiana and that during a calendar year: (1) controls or processes personal data of at least one hundred thousand (100,000) consumers who are Indiana residents; or (2) controls or processes personal data of at least twenty-five thousand (25,000) consumers who are Indiana residents and derives more than fifty percent (50%) of gross revenue from the sale of personal data.

in-tax.name: Indiana Department of Revenue, Bulletin 8
in-tax.what: Sales tax on computer services and web hosting
in-tax.quote: Web hosting is a form of IaaS and is considered a service, and therefore not subject to Indiana sales or use tax. Further, web design is a service not subject to sales and use tax as long as tangible personal property is not transferred as part of the transaction.

in-breach.name: Indiana Attorney General
in-breach.quote: The disclosure must be made without unreasonable delay ... Affected consumers following the discovery of the breach.

filing.line: A Florida LLC files its annual report on Sunbiz between 1 January and 1 May for $138.75; after 1 May the Division of Corporations adds a $400 late fee.

privacy.line: Part V of chapter 501 covers only companies with over $1 billion in global revenue that meet one more test, such as earning half of it from online advertising.

breach.line: Florida sets an outer limit for notice to each affected individual in the state, counted from the moment a breach is determined or suspected.

Florida.lead: For most Florida businesses the breach statute, not the billion-dollar privacy law, is the rule that governs what a site's forms collect.
Florida.crm: Florida's breach statute, § 501.171, applies to customer records in a CRM, so who can export them is worth deciding on day one.

fl-sunbiz.name: Florida Division of Corporations (Sunbiz)
fl-sunbiz.quote: The fee to file a limited liability company annual report is $138.75 if filed between January 1st and May 1st. After May 1st the limited liability company will be subject to a $400 late fee.

fl-dbr.name: Florida Legislature, § 501.702
fl-dbr.what: Florida Digital Bill of Rights: who is a controller
fl-dbr.quote: 5. Makes in excess of $1 billion in global gross annual revenues; and 6. Satisfies at least one of the following: a. Derives 50 percent or more of its global gross annual revenues from the sale of advertisements online

fl-breach.name: Florida Legislature, § 501.171
fl-breach.quote: A covered entity shall give notice to each individual in this state ... no later than 30 days after the determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred

Florida.crmLead: The privacy law reaches only billion-dollar companies, while the breach statute covers any business holding Floridians' personal information.

filing.line: Georgia LLCs and corporations renew with the Secretary of State's Corporations Division by April 1, from 1 January onward, for $60, online through eCorp.

breach.line: Businesses that keep unencrypted personal records must tell affected Georgians in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay.

Georgia.lead: Georgia's April registration and its breach statute are the two state rules a site's legal name and its contact forms answer to.
Georgia.crm: Georgia's breach statute, O.C.G.A. § 10-1-912, applies to unencrypted customer records, so field encryption and export rights in a CRM are worth settling early.

ga-sos.name: Georgia Secretary of State, Corporations Division
ga-sos.what: How to file an annual registration
ga-sos.quote: Entity annual registrations are due by April 1st of each year it is due, but may be filed as early as January 1st. ... Annual Registration (Profit Corp., Professional Corp., Benefit Corp., LLC, LP, LLLP, Trust Estate) $60.00 $60.00

ga-breach.name: Georgia Department of Law, Consumer Protection Division
ga-breach.what: Getting notified following a data breach
ga-breach.quote: Georgia Law O.C.G.A. § 10-1-912 requires businesses who collect, transmit or maintain unencrypted digital records ... in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay.

Georgia.crmLead: The statute covers unencrypted records, so encrypting sensitive fields changes what a breach of the org legally means.

filing.h3: The Corporation Commission, not the SOS
filing.line: Arizona entities file with the Arizona Corporation Commission, and LLCs file no annual report there; only corporations do.

breach.line: Once an investigation confirms a breach, the business that owns the data has a fixed window in the statute to notify the people affected.

Arizona.lead: Arizona's quirks start at filing: the Corporation Commission keeps the entity record, and its record is where a site's legal name should match.
Arizona.crm: Arizona's breach statute, A.R.S. § 18-552, sets a fixed window once a breach of the customer data is confirmed, which a CRM's audit trail helps establish.

az-acc.name: Arizona Corporation Commission
az-acc.quote: Do LLCs file annual reports? No, LLCs are not required to file annual reports. Only corporations are required to file annual reports.

az-breach.name: Arizona State Legislature, A.R.S. § 18-552
az-breach.what: Notification of a security system breach
az-breach.quote: If the investigation results in a determination that there has been a security system breach, the person that owns or licenses the computerized data, within forty-five days after the determination, shall: 1. Notify the individuals affected

filing.line: Texas entities file with the Secretary of State, whose SOSPortal replaced SOSDirect on 29 September 2026, bringing filing, ordering and searching together into a single, streamlined platform.

privacy.h3: Texas Data Privacy and Security Act
privacy.line: In force since 1 July 2024, it exempts most businesses that meet the SBA's small-business definition, except that they must get consent before selling sensitive data.

tax.line: Comptroller Publication 94-127 lists creating a web page and providing server space as taxable data processing, so Texas build invoices carry a sales tax question.

breach.h3: Reporting a breach to the Attorney General
breach.line: A breach affecting 250 or more Texans must be reported to the Office of the Attorney General as soon as practicable.

Texas.lead: In Texas the state's own tax guidance names web pages as data processing, so the proposal should separate design, build and hosting.
Texas.crm: Texas makes a breach affecting 250 or more Texans reportable to the Attorney General, so a CRM's export log is evidence worth keeping.

tx-sos.name: Texas Secretary of State
tx-sos.quote: We are pleased to announce the launch of SOSPortal, our new Business Filing system, on September 29, 2026. SOSPortal will replace both SOSDirect and SOSUpload, bringing filing, ordering, and searching together into a single, streamlined platform.

tx-ag.name: Office of the Texas Attorney General
tx-ag.what: Texas Data Privacy and Security Act
tx-ag.quote: Small businesses (as defined by the federal Small Business Administration) are generally exempt from the Act, except that if a small business sells the sensitive data of a consumer, it must first obtain the consumer’s consent.

tx-tax.name: Texas Comptroller, Publication 94-127
tx-tax.quote: Data processing is a service performed with a computer using the customer's data. ... Examples of taxable services are: ... Internet services: creating web (home) page and providing server space.

tx-breach.name: Office of the Texas Attorney General
tx-breach.quote: Texas law requires businesses and organizations that experience a data breach of system security that affects 250 or more Texans to report that breach to the Office of the Texas Attorney General as soon as practicably possible and no later than 30 days after the discovery of the breach. Businesses and organizations must also provide notice of the breach to affected consumers.

Texas.crmLead: Most small businesses are exempt from the Texas privacy act, but a breach touching 250 or more Texans still goes to the Attorney General.

filing.line: A California LLC files Form LLC-12 on bizfile Online with the Secretary of State soon after registering and every two years after, for $20.

privacy.line: The California Privacy Protection Agency lists the tests: $26.625 million or more in revenue, data of 100,000 residents or households, or half of revenue from selling or sharing it.

tax.h3: Web design and California sales tax
tax.line: CDTFA Publication 37 says designing, creating or hosting a website is generally not taxable, unless something tangible, such as printed copy or storage media, is delivered.

breach.line: A business must disclose a breach to affected Californians, and a notice that goes to more than 500 residents is also sent to the Attorney General.

California.lead: California is the state where a covered business's site most often needs a privacy notice, opt-out links and a record of each request.
California.crm: Under the CCPA a covered business must find and act on one person's records on request, so Salesforce data must be linked, not scattered.

ca-sos.name: California Secretary of State
ca-sos.quote: Statement of Information: Due within 90 days of initial registration and every two years thereafter. Form LLC-12 (PDF) $20.00

ca-cppa.name: California Privacy Protection Agency
ca-cppa.what: Frequently asked questions: who the CCPA applies to
ca-cppa.quote: Have a gross annual revenue of $26.625 million or more (effective January 1, 2025) for the preceding calendar year; Buy, sell, or share the personal information of 100,000 or more California residents or households; or Derive 50% or more of their annual revenue from selling or sharing California residents' personal information.

ca-tax.name: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration, Publication 37
ca-tax.what: Graphic design, website and related services
ca-tax.quote: Generally, the design, creation, or hosting of a website is not taxable because the product you provide is electronic, not tangible. ... However, if you deliver a tangible product to your customer, whether on storage media or in printed copy, your charges for creating the website may be taxable.

ca-breach.name: California Legislative Information, Civil Code § 1798.82
ca-breach.quote: Subject to subparagraph (B), the disclosure required by this subdivision shall be made within 30 calendar days of discovery or notification of the data breach.

California.crmLead: Requests to know or delete arrive per person, so a California org needs one linked record per customer, not copies across objects.

filing.line: A Michigan LLC files an annual statement with LARA's Corporations Division by February 15, for $25, through the MiBusiness Registry Portal.

breach.line: Unless a breach is unlikely to cause substantial loss, injury or identity theft, each affected Michigan resident must be told without unreasonable delay.

Michigan.lead: Michigan's February statement and its breach statute are the state rules a site's footer details and contact forms answer to.
Michigan.crm: Michigan's MCL 445.72 makes the likely harm of a breach the test for notice, which is easier to judge when a CRM records who opened which record.

mi-lara.name: Michigan LARA, Corporations Division
mi-lara.quote: Due Date: February 15 each year after organization/qualification. However, if the limited liability company is formed/qualified after September 30, it is not required to file an annual statement on February 15 of the year immediately succeeding its formation. ... LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANIES Fee: $25.00

mi-breach.name: Michigan Legislature, MCL 445.72
mi-breach.quote: A person or agency shall provide any notice required under this section without unreasonable delay.

tax.h3: Website creation and Ohio sales tax
tax.line: The Ohio Department of Taxation's taxability list says website creation is not taxable when it is billed as a personal service.

breach.line: When a breach creates a material risk of identity theft or fraud, Ohio residents must be told in the most expedient time possible, within the statute's limit.

Ohio.lead: In Ohio how the build is billed matters: the state's own taxability list ties the answer to billing it as a personal service.
Ohio.crm: Ohio's R.C. 1349.19 turns on a material risk of identity theft or fraud, so knowing exactly which CRM fields were exposed decides the notice.

oh-tax.name: Ohio Department of Taxation
oh-tax.what: Sales and use tax: taxability list
oh-tax.quote: Website Creation: Not taxable when billed as a personal service.

oh-breach.name: Ohio Laws and Administrative Rules, R.C. 1349.19
oh-breach.what: Private disclosure of a security breach
oh-breach.quote: The person shall make the disclosure described in division (B)(1) of this section in the most expedient time possible but not later than forty-five days following its discovery or notification of the breach in the security of the system

filing.line: Under LLC Law § 206 a new New York LLC publishes its formation in two newspapers for six weeks, then files a certificate of publication with the Department of State for $50.

tax.line: Advisory Opinion TSB-A-20(70)S found that website development services are not among New York's enumerated taxable services; an opinion binds only the business that asked.

breach.line: Since the SHIELD Act, a business holding New Yorkers' private information must notify them after a breach within the statute's outer limit.

New York.lead: New York adds a step most states skip: the newspaper publication a new LLC must finish, or its authority to do business is suspended.
New York.crm: New York's SHIELD Act amendments to GBL § 899-aa cover private information a CRM holds, so field-level access and encryption deserve a decision up front.

ny-dos.name: New York Department of State, Division of Corporations
ny-dos.what: LLC articles of organization and publication
ny-dos.quote: The fee for filing the Articles of Organization is $200. ... Failure to publish and file the Certificate of Publication with the Department of State within 120 days

ny-tax.name: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
ny-tax.quote: Website development services, including consulting, designing and website creation, are not enumerated services subject to New York State and local sales and compensating use taxes. See Tax Law § 1105(c); TSB-A-01(21)S.

ny-breach.name: New York State Senate, General Business Law § 899-aa
ny-breach.quote: shall disclose any breach of the security of the system following discovery or notification of the breach ... provided that such notification shall be made within thirty days after the breach has been discovered

New York.crmLead: A breach of New Yorkers' private information starts a notice duty with a firm outer limit, so access settings come before the first data load.
New York.stateLede: Outside the city, the state's own rules decide two things a site states: the LLC's published name and how the build is taxed.

filing.line: DC entities file with DLCP's Corporations Division through CorpOnline; the biennial report is due by April 1, $300 for a for-profit, with a $100 late fee.

breach.line: Affected DC residents must be told promptly, and the Attorney General's office too when a breach reaches 50 or more residents.

District of Columbia.lead: In DC the license and the corporate record both sit with DLCP, and the breach rule reaches the Attorney General at a low threshold.
District of Columbia.crm: DC's § 28-3852 brings in the Attorney General once 50 residents' records are affected, a low bar for any membership or donor database.

dc-dlcp.name: DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection
dc-dlcp.quote: For-profit entities: $300 ... Late fee (filed after April 1 of the year due): $100 for-profit, $50 non-profit

dc-breach.name: Council of the District of Columbia, D.C. Code § 28-3852
dc-breach.quote: shall promptly notify any District of Columbia resident whose personal information was included in the breach ... shall promptly provide written notice of the breach of the security of the system to the Office of the Attorney General

District of Columbia.crmLead: Membership and donor records count as personal information, so access, encryption and export rights in Salesforce are settled before the first import.

filing.h3: The yearly report and its deadline
filing.line: A New Jersey business files its annual report with the Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services by the last day of its formation month, for $75; skipping it can lead to revocation.

privacy.h3: The Data Privacy Act, P.L.2023, c.266
privacy.line: The state's privacy act covers businesses that handle data of 100,000 consumers in the state, not counting payment-only data, or 25,000 while earning revenue from selling it.

breach.line: Before telling customers, a New Jersey business reports a breach to the Division of State Police, then notifies residents without unreasonable delay.

New Jersey.lead: The state's privacy act gives a covered business's site a privacy notice and opt-out route to carry, on top of the yearly report.
New Jersey.crm: New Jersey's Data Privacy Act reaches the customer records in a Salesforce org above its thresholds, and a breach goes to the State Police first.

nj-rev.name: Business.NJ.gov (Division of Revenue and Enterprise Services)
nj-rev.quote: The report is due every year on the last day of the month, in the month in which you completed your business formation ... submitting a $75 filing fee. ... Failure to file can result in the revocation of your business.

nj-dpa.name: New Jersey Legislature, P.L.2023, c.266
nj-dpa.quote: the provisions of P.L.2023, c.266 (C.56:8-166.4 et seq.) shall only apply to controllers that conduct business in the State ... control or process the personal data of at least 100,000 consumers, ... control or process the personal data of at least 25,000 consumers and the controller derives revenue, ... This act shall take effect on the 365th day following the date of enactment

nj-breach.name: New Jersey Division of Consumer Affairs
nj-breach.quote: The disclosure to a customer shall be made in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay ... shall, in advance of the disclosure to the customer, report the breach of security and any information pertaining to the breach to the Division of State Police in the Department of Law and Public Safety

filing.h3: Delaware's LLC tax, not a report
filing.line: Delaware LLCs file no annual report; they pay the Division of Corporations a $400 annual tax on or before June 1, with a $200 penalty and interest if late.

privacy.line: In force since 1 January 2025, it starts at a lower bar than most: data of 35,000 consumers, or 10,000 when selling data is a large share of revenue.

breach.line: Affected Delawareans must be told without unreasonable delay, and the Attorney General as well when more than 500 residents are affected.

Delaware.lead: Delaware's privacy act starts at 35,000 consumers, so even a mid-sized site's mailing list can bring a privacy notice and opt-out route into scope.
Delaware.crm: Delaware's privacy act starts at 35,000 consumers, a size many CRM contact lists reach, so consent fields belong in the data model.

de-corp.name: Delaware Division of Corporations
de-corp.what: Annual franchise tax instructions for LLCs
de-corp.quote: are required to pay an annual tax of $400.00 ... The annual taxes for the prior year are due on or before June 1st. ... Failure to pay the required annual taxes will result in a penalty of $200.00 plus 1.5% interest per month ... There is no requirement to file an Annual Report.

de-ag.name: Delaware Department of Justice
de-ag.quote: The DPDP Act takes effect on January 1, 2025. ... at least 35,000 consumers; or ... 10,000 or more consumers and derived over 20% of gross revenue from the sale of personal data.

de-breach.name: Delaware Code, Title 6, § 12B-102
de-breach.what: Notice of a breach of security
de-breach.quote: not later than 60 days after determination of the breach of security ... the affected number of Delaware residents to be notified exceeds 500 residents ... also provide notice of the breach of security to the Attorney General

filing.line: Since 1 January 2025 most domestic and foreign filing associations file a yearly report with the Department of State through Business Filing Services; LLCs file by September 30, and business corporations pay $7.

breach.line: An entity that keeps computerized personal information must notify affected Pennsylvanians of a breach once it is determined, under the 2005 act as amended in 2022.

Pennsylvania.lead: The state's annual report is new, so an entity record that lapsed since 2025 is worth checking before a site prints the legal name.
Pennsylvania.crm: Pennsylvania's breach notification act, amended in 2022, covers the personal information a Salesforce org stores for Pennsylvania customers.
Pennsylvania.crmLead: Missing Pennsylvania's new annual report can end an entity's good standing, so account records in Salesforce should match the Department of State.

pa-dos.name: Pennsylvania Department of State
pa-dos.quote: Beginning in 2025, most domestic and foreign filing associations are required to file an Annual Report [DSCB:15-146]. ... The annual report requirement begins on January 1, 2025. The deadline for limited liability companies (domestic and foreign) is September 30. The fee for the new Annual Report is $7 for business corporations, limited liability companies (LLCs)...

pa-breach.name: Pennsylvania General Assembly
pa-breach.what: Breach of Personal Information Notification Act
pa-breach.quote: An entity that maintains, stores or manages computerized data that includes personal information shall provide notice of any breach of the security of the system following determination of the breach of the security of the system to any resident of this Commonwealth whose unencrypted and unredacted personal information was or is reasonably believed to have been accessed and acquired by an unauthorized person. ... When notice of the breach of the security of the system under this section must be given to more than 500 affected individuals in this Commonwealth, notice shall be made concurrently to the Office of Attorney General.

filing.line: A North Carolina LLC files its first annual report with the Secretary of State by April 15 of the year after it forms, and every April 15 after, for $200.

breach.line: Any business that owns or licenses North Carolinians' personal information, in any form, must give notice of a security breach without unreasonable delay.

North Carolina.lead: North Carolina's breach statute covers personal information in any form, paper included, so forms and the inbox behind them both count.
North Carolina.crm: North Carolina's G.S. 75-65 covers personal information in any form, so exports and printed reports from a CRM count too.

nc-sos.name: North Carolina Secretary of State
nc-sos.quote: The first annual report is due on April 15th of the year following the creation year and every year thereafter on or before April 15th. ... If filed electronically, there is a $3.00 transaction fee for credit cards.

nc-breach.name: North Carolina General Assembly, G.S. 75-65
nc-breach.quote: Any business that owns or licenses personal information of residents of North Carolina or any business that conducts business in North Carolina that owns or licenses personal information in any form (whether computerized, paper, or otherwise) shall provide notice to the affected person that there has been a security breach following discovery or notification of the breach.

filing.line: Colorado entities file a periodic report online with the Secretary of State, from two months before to two months after their report month, for $25.

privacy.line: In force since 1 July 2023, it covers businesses that process data of more than 100,000 Coloradans a year, or that profit from selling personal data.

breach.line: The Attorney General's guidance sets the most expedient time possible, with a firm outer limit from the date a breach is determined.

Colorado.lead: Colorado's privacy act gives a covered business's site a privacy notice and opt-out requests to honor, both built into the front end.
Colorado.crm: The Colorado Privacy Act has applied since 1 July 2023, reaching the customer records in a Salesforce org above its thresholds.
Colorado.crmLead: Colorado's breach rule counts from the day a breach is determined, so a CRM's login and export history shortens the investigation.

co-sos.name: Colorado Secretary of State
co-sos.quote: The Periodic Report can be filed two months prior to the Periodic Report month or two months after without any penalty. The Periodic Report must be filed electronically through our website.

co-ag.name: Colorado Attorney General
co-ag.quote: On July 7, 2021, Governor Polis signed Senate Bill 21-190: Protect Personal Data Privacy establishing the Colorado Privacy Act (CPA). The CPA is a part of the State of Colorado's Consumer Protection Act and went into effect July 1, 2023. The law applies to entities, including nonprofits, that conduct business in Colorado or deliver commercial products or services targeted to residents of Colorado; AND either: Process the personal data of more than 100,000 individuals in any calendar year; or Derive revenue or receive discounts on goods or services in exchange for the sale of personal data of 25,000 or more individuals.

co-breach.name: Colorado Attorney General
co-breach.quote: You must provide notice in the most expedient time possible, without unreasonable delay, and within 30 days after the date of determination that a security breach has occurred. See section 6-1-716, C.R.S.

filing.line: Maryland entities file Form 1 with the State Department of Assessments and Taxation through Maryland Business Express by April 15; the LLC fee is $300.

privacy.line: In force since 1 October 2025, it starts at data of 35,000 Maryland consumers, not counting payment-only data, or fewer when selling data drives revenue.

tax.line: Since 1 July 2025 Maryland taxes data and IT services at 3%, and the Comptroller's technical bulletin lists custom webpage design services among them.

breach.line: Com. Law § 14-3504 requires reasonable protection of Maryland consumers' personal information and notice when it is breached.

Maryland.lead: Maryland changed twice in 2025: a 3% tax that names webpage design, and a privacy act that starts at 35,000 consumers.

md-sdat.name: Maryland State Department of Assessments and Taxation
md-sdat.quote: File online on or before April 15, 2025, at BusinessExpress.Maryland.gov or send the fillable form and payment to: ... The Form 1 Business Entity Annual Report and Personal Property Return is due on or before April 15, 2025.

md-odpa.name: Maryland General Assembly, Com. Law § 14-4702
md-odpa.what: Maryland Online Data Privacy Act: applicability
md-odpa.quote: This subtitle applies to a person that conducts business in the State or provides products or services that are targeted to residents of the State, and that during the preceding calendar year did any of the following: (1) Controlled or processed the personal data of at least 35,000 consumers, excluding personal data controlled or processed solely for the purpose of completing a payment transaction; or (2) Controlled or processed the personal data of at least 10,000 consumers and derived more than 20% of its gross revenue from the sale of personal data.

md-tax.name: Comptroller of Maryland, technical bulletin
md-tax.what: Sales and use tax on data and IT services
md-tax.quote: Effective July 1, 2025, sales of a data or information technology service described under NAICS sectors 518 or 519 ... The law imposes a 3.0% sales and use tax rate on a sale of these services. [Section IV.C, NAICS subsector 5415:] Custom webpage design services

md-breach.name: Office of the Maryland Attorney General
md-breach.what: Guidelines for the Personal Information Protection Act
md-breach.quote: The Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA), Md. Code Ann. Comm. Law 14-3504, was enacted to make sure that Maryland consumers' personal identifying information is reasonably protected, and if it is compromised, they are notified so that they can take steps to protect themselves. In the event of a security breach, notice must be given to consumers with 45 days.

filing.line: A Massachusetts LLC files its annual report with the Corporations Division by the anniversary of its certificate of organization, and the fee is $500.

breach.line: Anyone holding personal information about a Massachusetts resident must give notice as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay after a breach.

Massachusetts.lead: The Massachusetts breach law reaches anyone holding a resident's personal information, which includes the enquiries a site's forms collect.
Massachusetts.crm: Chapter 93H covers personal information about Massachusetts residents wherever it is held, including the contacts and cases in a Salesforce org.
Massachusetts.crmLead: Chapter 93H applies to any holder of residents' data, so field-level access in Salesforce is a compliance setting, not only a convenience.

ma-sec.name: Secretary of the Commonwealth, Corporations Division
ma-sec.quote: Each limited liability company shall file an annual report with the Division on or before the anniversary date of the filing of its original certificate of organization. ... The annual report shall be accompanied by a fee of $500.

ma-breach.name: Massachusetts Legislature, M.G.L. c. 93H, § 3
ma-breach.quote: A person or agency that owns or licenses data that includes personal information about a resident of the commonwealth, shall provide notice, as soon as practicable and without unreasonable delay, when such person or agency (1) knows or has reason to know of a breach of security ... to the attorney general, the director of consumer affairs and business regulation and to such resident, in accordance with this chapter.

filing.line: An Illinois LLC delivers Form LLC-50.1 to the Secretary of State before its anniversary month, for $75; a $100 penalty follows if it is late.

breach.line: Any data collector holding an Illinois resident's personal information must notify that resident of a breach at no charge.

Illinois.lead: The Illinois Personal Information Protection Act makes any data collector notify residents of a breach, which covers what a site's forms gather.
Illinois.crm: The Illinois Personal Information Protection Act makes any data collector notify residents of a breach, Salesforce orgs included.
Illinois.crmLead: The act applies to any data collector, so the export rights and API users on an org deserve the same review as staff logins.

il-sos.name: Illinois General Assembly, 805 ILCS 180/50-1
il-sos.quote: The annual report, together with all fees and charges prescribed by this Act, shall be delivered to the Secretary of State within 60 days immediately preceding the first day of the anniversary month.

il-breach.name: Illinois General Assembly, 815 ILCS 530/10
il-breach.quote: Any data collector that owns or licenses personal information concerning an Illinois resident shall notify the resident at no charge that there has been a breach of the security of the system data following discovery or notification of the breach. The disclosure notification shall be made in the most expedient time possible and without unreasonable delay...

filing.line: Washington entities file an annual report through the Secretary of State's Corporations and Charities Filing System by the last day of their formation month; LLCs pay $70.

privacy.line: Washington's consumer health data law applied from 31 March 2024, and from 30 June 2024 for small businesses, to health-related data a site or app collects.

tax.line: Since 1 October 2025, under ESSB 5814, website design, development and support are retail sales in Washington; hosting and domains are not. The Department of Revenue says it is in ongoing legal proceedings over how these services are classified.

breach.line: Washington requires notice in the most expedient time possible after a breach, with a firm outer limit set in the statute.

Washington.lead: Washington now taxes website development itself, and its health data law reaches any site that collects health-related details.
Washington.crm: The My Health My Data Act reaches health-related details a CRM stores, a wider net than most states draw.
Washington.crmLead: Health-related notes in a contact or case record can bring an org under the Act, so field design matters from the start.

wa-sos.name: Washington Secretary of State
wa-sos.quote: An Annual Report is due by the expiration date, which is the last day of the month in which the business was first formed. $70 – Profit Business Entity Types, including LLC

wa-ag.name: Washington State Office of the Attorney General
wa-ag.what: Protecting Washingtonians' personal health data and privacy
wa-ag.quote: The Washington My Health My Data Act (HB 1155) passed the Washington State Legislature on April 17, 2023, and was signed into law by Governor Jay Inslee on April 27, 2023. Regulated entities that are not small businesses must comply with sections 4 through 9 beginning March 31, 2024. Small businesses, as defined in the Act, must comply with sections 4 through 9 beginning June 30, 2024.

wa-tax.name: Washington Department of Revenue
wa-tax.what: Services newly subject to retail sales tax
wa-tax.quote: As of Oct. 1, 2025, a new law (ESSB 5814) requires that certain services now be taxed when sold. [Table row] Custom website development - Included: Website design, development, and support. Not included: Web hosting and domain registration services. ... Notice regarding legal proceedings The Washington Department of Revenue (DOR) is currently involved in ongoing legal proceedings regarding the classification of services newly subject to retail sales tax

wa-breach.name: Washington State Office of the Attorney General
wa-breach.quote: Washington has two data breach notification laws: RCW 19.255 applies to individuals and businesses ... In general, notification must be made "in the most expedient time possible" and within 30 days after the breach was discovered. If a data breach affects more than 500 Washington residents, notification must also be provided to the Attorney General's Office...

license.line: Louisville requires no local business license, but a new business registers with the Louisville Metro Revenue Commission, the Jefferson County Clerk and the Commonwealth before it earns income.

Louisville.lede: Louisville trades a city license for three registrations, and Kentucky's sales tax reaches website design itself.

city.name: Louisville Metro Revenue Commission
city.what: Frequently asked questions: starting a new business
city.quote: For an individual or business entity to start a new business there is no local business license required. However, new businesses must be registered with the Louisville Metro Revenue Commission (LMRC), Jefferson County Clerk's Office and the Commonwealth of Kentucky. Registration should take place before earning income or business activity begins.

license.h3: No general license, but an occupancy permit
license.line: The City of Milwaukee issues no general business license, only licenses for particular trades, and every business that occupies premises in the city needs an occupancy permit.

Milwaukee.lede: Milwaukee licenses trades rather than businesses, and Wisconsin keeps website design outside its sales tax.

city.name: City of Milwaukee License Division
city.quote: The City of Milwaukee does not issue general business licenses. Licenses are required for specific types of businesses. ... An occupancy permit is required for all businesses occupying premises in the city of Milwaukee.

license.line: Businesses subject to the Portland Business License Tax register for a Revenue Division account, and the same registration covers the Multnomah County Business Income Tax.

Portland.lede: Portland asks for a tax account rather than a license, and Oregon's privacy act sets what the site must disclose.

city.name: City of Portland Revenue Division
city.quote: Businesses that are subject to the Portland Business License Tax ... Multnomah County Business Income Tax ... are required to register for a Revenue Division tax account.

license.h3: A Salt Lake City business license
license.line: Anyone engaging in business in Salt Lake City, permanently or temporarily, needs a city business license from the Finance Department's Business Licensing office.

Salt Lake City.lede: Salt Lake City licenses every business inside its limits, and Utah's privacy act starts at a revenue floor.

city.name: Salt Lake City Business Licensing
city.quote: If you engage in any business – either permanently or temporarily – within the corporate limits of Salt Lake City

license.line: The city's how-to page says that to run a business in Minneapolis you need a business license, issued by its Business Licensing office.

Minneapolis.lede: Minneapolis licensing starts with the city's own office, and Minnesota's privacy act is the newest rule a site must meet.

city.name: City of Minneapolis Business Licensing
city.what: How to apply for a business license
city.quote: To run a business in Minneapolis, you need a business license.

license.line: Indianapolis's Department of Business and Neighborhood Services publishes license rules business type by business type rather than one general license.

Indianapolis.lede: Indianapolis licenses by trade, and Indiana's privacy act began on 1 January 2026.

city.name: City of Indianapolis, Business and Neighborhood Services
city.quote: On this page, you'll find general instructions for business license applications, followed by licensing requirements for businesses by type.

license.line: A business inside Tampa's city limits needs a City of Tampa Business Tax Receipt from the Business Tax Division and a Hillsborough County receipt from the Tax Collector.

Tampa.lede: Tampa asks for two business tax receipts, one city and one county, before a business opens.

city.name: City of Tampa Business Tax Division
city.quote: The Business Tax Division is part of the City of Tampa's Neighborhood Empowerment Department ... responsible for the issuance and collection for all Business Tax Receipts.

license.line: Every business operating within Atlanta's city limits needs an Occupational Tax Certificate from the Office of Revenue, applied for through the ATLBIZ portal; certificates cannot be transferred.

Atlanta.lede: Atlanta requires an occupational tax certificate of every business in its limits, and Georgia renews entities each April.

city.name: City of Atlanta Office of Revenue
city.what: Apply for a new business occupational tax certificate
city.quote: An Occupational Tax Certificate is required of all businesses operating within the city limits of Atlanta and are not transferable.

license.line: A business with taxable activities in Phoenix needs a transaction privilege (sales) tax license from the city's Finance Department: a $50 licence fee at the start, then a $50 renewal fee due each 1 January.

Phoenix.lede: Phoenix licenses through its transaction privilege tax, and Arizona's corporate record sits with the Corporation Commission.

city.name: City of Phoenix Finance Department
city.quote: A non-refundable $50.00 license fee is due within 30 days of your business's start date in the first year of application. ... Each year after that, a $50.00 renewal fee is due on January 1st.

license.line: The City of Houston's own new-business guide says there is no general business license issued by the city; permits follow the activity.

Houston.lede: Houston issues no general business license, so Texas filings and tax rules carry more of the weight.

city.name: City of Houston Office of Business Opportunity
city.quote: THERE IS NO GENERAL BUSINESS LICENSE ISSUED BY THE CITY OF HOUSTON.

license.line: The city's quick reference guide says most commercial businesses in Dallas may not open or occupy a space without a Certificate of Occupancy, which also flags the licenses needed.

Dallas.lede: Dallas starts with a certificate of occupancy for the space, and Texas taxes web pages as data processing.

city.name: City of Dallas Office of Economic Development
city.quote: Most commercial businesses may not operate their business nor occupy the space without first obtaining a Certificate of Occupancy (CO). ... In most cases, you will be informed of the required licenses when you apply for your certificate of occupancy.

license.line: The city notes that Texas requires no general business license, while most businesses there still need permits or licenses tied to their type and location.

Austin.lede: Permits here follow the business type, and the Texas Comptroller treats web page creation as data processing.

city.name: City of Austin Economic Development
city.quote: the State of Texas does not require a general "business" license; however, there are a number of regulatory agencies that have licensing and permitting requirements based on the type of service, or products associated with your business. ... Most businesses in Austin do require permits and/or licenses. This varies depending on your business type, location, and activites.

license.line: Every business operating in San Diego needs a Business Tax Certificate from the City Treasurer, home-based businesses, the self-employed and independent contractors included.

San Diego.lede: San Diego requires a business tax certificate of every business, and California's privacy law sets the site's disclosures.

city.name: City of San Diego Office of the City Treasurer
city.quote: All businesses operating in the City of San Diego are required to obtain a Business Tax Certificate. This includes home-based businesses, self-employed persons and independent contractors.

license.line: Anyone engaged in business in the City of Los Angeles needs a Tax Registration Certificate from the Office of Finance, and working in the city seven or more days a year counts.

Los Angeles.lede: Los Angeles registers every business for its business tax, and the CCPA sets what a covered site must disclose.

city.name: City of Los Angeles Office of Finance
city.what: Business tax FAQ and BTRC registration
city.quote: This section requires that every person engaged in any trade, calling, occupation, vocation, profession or other means of livelihood in the City of Los Angeles, must obtain a Tax Registration Certificate (TRC) and pay the required business tax due ... You are considered to be engaged in business in the City of Los Angeles when you physically perform work within the City of Los Angeles for seven (7) or more days per year.

license.line: San Francisco's code requires every person doing business in the city to register with the Treasurer and Tax Collector soon after starting, taxable or not, and to renew each year by the end of February.

San Francisco.lede: San Francisco registers every business with the Treasurer each year, and California's privacy law covers the site above its thresholds.

city.name: Office of the Treasurer & Tax Collector, San Francisco
city.quote: San Francisco’s Business and Tax Regulations Code generally requires that every person engaging in business within the City, regardless of whether the business or person is subject to taxation, must register within 30 days after commencing business within the City.

license.h3: City income tax, not a general license
license.line: Residents conducting a business and non-residents conducting a business in Columbus must file an annual city return; all businesses except sole proprietorships file on Form BR-25.

Columbus.lede: Columbus asks for a city income tax return rather than a general license, and Ohio taxes web work by how it is billed.

city.name: City of Columbus, Division of Income Tax
city.quote: all residents conducting a business or non-residents conducting a business within the city must file an annual return ... All businesses, with the exception of sole proprietorships, file their city taxes using Form BR-25.

license.line: The city's MyCity Business tool gives each business a personalized list of the city, state and federal licenses and permits it needs.

New York.lede: New York City licenses by activity, and New York State adds a newspaper publication step for every new LLC.

city.name: NYC Business (MyCity)
city.what: Licenses and permits needed to run a business
city.quote: Use this tool to see your personalized list of City, State, and Federal licenses and permits needed to run your business.

license.line: DLCP issues the Basic Business License; consultants paid for their services file under the General Business category, and licenses run for two or four years.

Washington, DC.lede: DC's Basic Business License and its corporate filings both sit with DLCP.

city.name: DC Department of Licensing and Consumer Protection
city.quote: You need a Basic Business License (BBL) under the General Business category ... If you are conducting business to or from the District, a Basic Business License may be required ... All Basic Business Licenses (BBLs) are valid for two (2) years, or four (4) years unless otherwise specified.

license.line: Every business in the City of Miami needs a city Business Tax Receipt and a Miami-Dade County Local Business Tax Receipt.

Miami.lede: Miami asks for two business tax receipts, one from the city and one from Miami-Dade County.

city.name: City of Miami
city.quote: Every business needs to obtain a Business Tax Receipt to operate in the City (also known as an Occupational License). ... every business is also required to obtain a Miami-Dade County Local Business Tax Receipt.

license.line: Anyone with a place of business who performs work in Pittsburgh, even partly and even from outside the city, registers with the Treasurer for a City ID number under Chapter 258.

Pittsburgh.lede: Pittsburgh registers anyone who works in the city, and Pennsylvania now asks every entity for a yearly report.

city.name: City of Pittsburgh Department of Finance
city.quote: Every person having an office, factory, workshop, branch, warehouse, or other place of business ... located in the City or outside the City, who, during any tax year, performs work or renders services in whole or in part in the City, who has not previously registered, shall within fifteen (15) days, register with the Treasurer its name and address ... - Chapter 258 of the City Code. Your business is not registered until you receive a verification letter from the Department of Finance.

license.line: The City of Raleigh does not require a business license to operate within city limits; activity permits, such as for selling beer or wine, still apply.

Raleigh.lede: Raleigh asks for no city business license, so North Carolina's April report is the yearly filing that counts.

city.name: City of Raleigh
city.quote: The City of Raleigh does not require a business license to operate a business within Raleigh City limits.

license.h3: Licenses by type, and the OPT
license.line: Denver issues business licenses by type, a retail sales license to anyone selling taxable items, and registers businesses for the Occupational Privilege Tax when people work in the city.

Denver.lede: Denver licenses by business type and taxes work done in the city, and the Colorado Privacy Act shapes the site.

city.name: City and County of Denver, Treasury
city.quote: A business license and a special industry license may be required to conduct business in Denver. Register for Denver Occupational Privilege Tax (OPT) and report and remit that tax on time, if you or your employees perform services in Denver. Occupational Privilege Tax - $4.00 per month from employer and $5.75 per month from employee.

license.h3: Licenses by type, SDAT number first
license.line: Baltimore's Business Licensing Division issues licenses by business type, and every applicant first needs a State Department of Assessments and Taxation number.

Baltimore.lede: Baltimore licenses start with a state SDAT number, and Maryland now taxes custom webpage design at 3%.

city.name: Baltimore City Department of Consumer Protection and Business Licensing
city.quote: SDAT: Register for a State Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) number on the Maryland Business Express website. Certificate of Good Standing: Check and ensure your entity is in Good Standing via the Maryland Business Express website. Application Fee: Pay your application fee online.

license.line: A business trading in Boston under a name other than its legal name files a Business Certificate with the City Clerk, $65, renewed every four years.

Boston.lede: Boston asks for a business certificate whenever the trading name differs from the legal one, which is the name a site shows.

city.name: City of Boston, Office of the City Clerk
city.quote: You need a Business Certificate if you run your business under a name different from its legal name, sometimes also called "doing business as" (DBA), trade name, or assumed name. Filing fee : $65 Non-resident surcharge : an extra $35 if you don't live in Massachusetts but want to conduct business in the state ... You must renew your Business Certificate every four years, counting from the date you first registered with the City Clerk.

license.h3: A City of Chicago business license
license.line: Most business activities in Chicago need a city business license from the Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection, with listed exemptions.

Chicago.lede: Chicago licenses most business activity through one department, and the Illinois breach act covers what a site collects.

city.name: Chicago Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection
city.quote: The Chicago Department of Business Affairs and Consumer Protection (BACP) issues business licenses to businesses operating in Chicago. While most business activities taking place in Chicago require a City of Chicago business license, there are certain business license exemptions.

license.h3: The Seattle business license tax certificate
license.line: Anyone doing business in Seattle needs a business license tax certificate, renewed yearly; from 2026 it is not needed with $4,000 or less of Seattle income and no place of business there.

Seattle.lede: Seattle licenses nearly every business through its tax certificate, and Washington now taxes website development.

city.name: City of Seattle, Office of City Finance
city.quote: Anyone doing business in Seattle must have a Seattle business license tax certificate, also known as a business license or general business license. Effective 2026: Any person whose annual value of products, gross proceeds of sales, or gross income of the business in the City is equal to or less than $4,000 and who does not maintain a place of business within the City is not required to obtain a business license tax certificate.
